title: Account > Add-ons
note: A new group under Provider. "Add an add-on" first, then the installed ones in order: what each gives, in plain words, and its state. v1.1: "copies", never "streams"; the caption says what order does. OK opens an add-on's sheet; hold OK: Move, Turn off, Remove.

title: An add-on's sheet: Cinemeta
note: OK on Cinemeta. What it gives, an on/off switch, and one switch per catalog: its chip in Movies or Series. v1.1 (review M1): Home keeps its two rows, so catalogs live on Movies and Series only, and the catalog menu is gone.

title: Moving an add-on
note: Hold OK on a row, then Move: the row lifts (the Saved reorder model), ▲▼ move it, OK drops. Order decides whose details win, the order of catalog chips, and the tie-break between equal copies.

title: Add an add-on: four ways
note: OK on "Add an add-on". The Stremio account is first and marked Easiest: no typing, and it also carries add-ons that need setting up. v1.1 (review S17): the one thing he must know is said in his words: copies come from add-ons set up with a service like Real-Debrid.

title: Stremio sign-in: the code
note: Stremio's own TV sign-in (link.stremio.com, verified: a 4-letter code, a link and a QR). The phone does the typing; the TV asks every 3 s. The fallback is one press away and focused, so a stray OK is harmless.

title: Your Stremio add-ons
note: The answer to addonCollectionGet, in plain words. What airglow can't use is named once, with why, never as a broken row. v1.1 (review S20): an add-on known to give nothing playable (Public Domain Movies) starts unticked. One OK adds the ticked ones.

title: Stremio sign-in: email fallback
note: The fallback, from the code screen. Errors sit under the field that caused them, in chalk with the "!" (never red). Verified: Stremio answers "User not found" with wrongEmail for an unknown address.

title: Stremio's list, on the TV
note: Pick from Stremio's list (Cinemeta's addon_catalog, real data). v1.1 (review M3): no "Streams" chip: none of the 19 community stream add-ons gives copies of films (they are ratings, after-credits and warnings: "Extras"). One line says where copies come from. Subtitles are filtered to his languages, so focus lands on something he can use.

title: Send a link from your phone
note: For an add-on set up on a web page (most debrid ones), without a Stremio account. The TV app serves one small page on the home network (the page the first-run "Use your phone" sign-in was designed with, UI-SPEC 5.1). v1.1 (review S13): a 6-digit code, locked after 5 wrong tries.

title: Before adding: what it gives
note: Every way in ends here: airglow reads the manifest first and says what the add-on gives. Nothing is added without this OK. v1.1 (review S15): it says plainly that the add-on sees what he opens. A link that isn't an add-on gets a plain "That link isn't an add-on" instead.

title: An add-on that needs setting up
note: A configurable add-on with configurationRequired. The setup itself happens on the add-on's own page (Stremio's rule); airglow only carries the result back. v1.1 (review S8): while this is open and he is signed in to Stremio, airglow reads his collection every 5 s, so Install finishes it too. Nothing to press on the TV, so nothing is focused.

title: The page the TV serves to the phone
note: Not a TV screen: the one page the TV serves on the home network (http, port 8790, token in the link). Three states: paste and send, set up an add-on, sent. Phone text is 14 px and up; one column; big buttons.

title: Movies: an add-on catalog chip
note: Add-on catalogs are chips after the provider's, past a thin divider (the row scrolls). v1.1 (review M1): this is the only place catalogs show; Home is unchanged. On an add-on chip the grid is that catalog, in its own order; Filters becomes the catalog's own Genre list; Sort and Jump go (an add-on has no total).

title: Movies: hiding an add-on chip
note: v1.1 (review M1): hiding a catalog happens where it shows. Hold OK on an add-on chip: Hide this chip (focused, harmless: it comes back from the add-on's sheet), or the add-on's sheet itself.

title: Movies: the next page didn't come
note: Scrolled down a catalog. While a page is on its way the next row is flat surface-2 blocks (no shimmer) and focus stays where it is, even under key repeat. If the page fails, that row becomes this one inline card: the titles above stay, ▼ reaches Try again, and the full "isn't answering" card is kept for a first page that fails.

title: Movies: the add-on isn't answering
note: The add-on timed out (8 s) or sent no JSON. The card says whose fault, that the provider's movies are fine, and offers Try again (focused) and All movies. Nothing else on the screen changes.

title: Search: provider first, then add-ons
note: Real Cinemeta search for "dune". v1.1: titles not out yet are left out. The provider's matches are instant and come first; add-on results arrive under "From add-ons" with the add-on named. A title in both shows once, as the provider's (Dune: Part Two is the top result with its 4K from Northlight).

title: Title page: Play takes the best source
note: The Version pill names what Play will play: the best so far by the shared ranking (SPEC 5.0), here Northlight's 4K Blu-ray over the provider's checked 1080p. v1.1 (review M4): add-on copies are never opened before Play, so their pill and tags have no tick, only the dashed "the name says" look. The match is Sure (the provider copy's length agrees with Cinemeta's), so add-on copies may outrank it.

title: The Copies menu, provider and add-ons together
note: OK on the Version pill: the subtitles design's Copies menu, add-on copies in the same list, in the shared order (SPEC 5.0). v1.1: no add-on copy is ticked (never opened before Play, review M4); a name claiming Dolby Vision on a Blu-ray ranks and reads as HDR10 until checked (review S3: profile 7). Ticks only where airglow checked.

title: Play, while an add-on is still looking
note: v1.1 (review M2): the one pre-play wait shared with the subtitles design (SPEC 5.0.2): one 4 s budget from the press, one caption, whatever it is waiting for. Here an add-on hasn't answered and the best known isn't 4K. The pill shows with one copy while an add-on is still asking.

title: A title only add-ons have
note: Opened from a Cinemeta chip or Search. The same page: Cinemeta's details, Northlight's copies, More like this from both. One quiet line says the provider doesn't have it and where the details come from.

title: Copies when the match is only Likely
note: The provider copy isn't checked yet, so the IMDb match is only Likely (same name, same year). Add-on copies, even 4K, wait below the provider's under "might be another film", naming the film they are for. When the check finds the same length (±8%), the match becomes Sure and they move up.

title: Series: episodes from both
note: Episodes are the union of the provider's list and Cinemeta's (seasons 1 to 5 and Specials, real data). An episode only add-ons have is marked Add-on. The focused episode's best source sits at the right of its one-line summary; the pill by Resume is for S3 · E4.

title: Which film is this? (an unsure match)
note: Shared with the subtitles design: a provider title that matches more than one IMDb title (no year, two films called Dune) is never guessed. One pick serves add-on copies and downloaded subtitles. The closest length to this copy is focused (2 h 35 min). Real Cinemeta search.

title: No copy to play
note: Real: Public Domain Movies answers this film with one infoHash stream and no link. airglow hides torrents, so the page says plainly why there's nothing, names each add-on, and offers Look again (focused) instead of a Play that can't work.

title: Player: a copy stops, the next one takes over
note: The hand-over card wins over the diagnosis cards for add-on copies (review M6): it names the add-on, never "your provider". v1.1 (review S7): the next copy comes from another source when it can, so a 1-connection provider is never asked twice in a row. Live TV never hands over (the score delay rule).

title: Player: a copy that isn't ready yet
note: v1.1 (review M4): debrid add-ons answer an uncached copy with a short placeholder video. A copy under half the film's length (Cinemeta's runtime or the provider's) is "not ready": no progress, no "watched", no tick, and the next copy plays. It drops to the bottom of Copies for the session.

title: Player: Quality lists every copy
note: Options > Quality, the subtitles design's panel, with each copy's source. The playing add-on copy was checked when it started, so it has its tick now. The Blu-ray copy sent a placeholder (player-not-ready) and sits last, dimmed, for this session.

title: Player: Up next keeps the same source
note: bingeGroup: the next episode's copies are asked for 2 min before the end; the one with the same bingeGroup plays (same add-on, same quality). v1.1 (review S6): the player asks the app for it (need: next), since add-on episodes have no link until asked.

title: Add-ons that stopped working
note: Real: Archivio's link now opens a web page, so it reads "Not an add-on any more" (review nit); "Not answering" is kept for timeouts (Kestrel, 3 in 10 min, not asked again for 30 min). Public Domain Movies reads "Catalog only": its films are all torrents.
